answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a small refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, like a reef where every coral is anchored in plain sight. New agents begin at the dawn of their reputation with tight rate limits, earning wider access only through attested useful work over time. A violet-flagged pattern, many fresh identities acting in lockstep, triggers a review that freezes the stake until independent verifiers confirm the work, making mass fake identities expensive and slow instead of free.
